bibl.title: Distinct relationships of parietal and prefrontal cortices to evidence accumulation

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether parietal and frontal cortex relate to accumulating evidence in the same way, tested by asking what each region's firing rate says about the value of the accumulator at each moment
span.quote: Here we develop a generalizable method to measure tuning curves that specify the relationship between neural responses and mentally-accumulated evidence, and apply it to distinguish the encoding of decision variables in posterior parietal cortex (PPC) and prefrontal cortex (frontal orienting fields, FOF).

span.label: whether frontal premotor activity participates in the graded accumulation of evidence or only in converting it into a discrete choice
span.quote: Contrary to current views 3 , 5 , 7 – 9 , this suggests that premotor activity in frontal cortex does not play a role in the accumulation process, but instead has a more categorical function, such as transforming accumulated evidence into a discrete choice.

span.label: parietal cortex encodes the accumulator as a graded value while frontal cortex encodes the sign of it, and silencing frontal cortex changes behaviour only at the end of the stimulus
span.quote: Classical analyses uncovered correlates of accumulating evidence, similar to previous observations in primates and also similar across the two regions. However, tuning curve assays revealed that while the PPC encodes a graded value of the accumulating evidence, the FOF has a more categorical encoding that indicates, throughout the trial, the decision provisionally favored by the evidence accumulated so far.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: However, tuning curve assays revealed that while the PPC encodes a graded value of the accumulating evidence, the FOF has a more categorical encoding that indicates, throughout the trial, the decision provisionally favored by the evidence accumulated so far.

span.label: evidence accumulation in perceptual decision-making
span.quote: Gradual accumulation of evidence is thought to be fundamental for decision-making, and its neural correlates have been found in multiple brain regions 1 – 8 .

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: We recorded the firing rates of neurons in PPC and FOF from rats performing a perceptual decision-making task.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the FOF does not integrate evidence; it reads out the sign of an accumulator computed upstream and converts it into a discrete motor plan at the moment the go signal could arrive, which is why perturbing it matters only at the end of the stimulus
span.quote: Contrary to current views 3 , 5 , 7 – 9 , this suggests that premotor activity in frontal cortex does not play a role in the accumulation process, but instead has a more categorical function, such as transforming accumulated evidence into a discrete choice.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: unilateral FOF silencing biases behavior by flipping already-categorized contralateral choices into ipsilateral ones, rather than by corrupting the accumulation itself
span.quote: We defined “post-categorization bias” as a process that takes a fraction of the trials categorized as choices contralateral to the inactivated side of the brain, and converts them into ipsilateral choices.

span.label: parietal firing answers what the value of the accumulated evidence is, through a graded map that is stable across time
span.quote: This analysis revealed that PPC encoded the accumulator’s evolving value a(t) using a graded map that is stable across time ( Fig. 3a ). A similar encoding was observed in monkey PPC, albeit using a task that did not require a temporal accumulation strategy 17 . Thus, during decision formation, firing rates in PPC change over time as the accumulated evidence changes, but at any timepoint the graded value of the accumulator is encoded, by a fixed map, into a graded firing rate. In this way, the firing rate provides the answer to the question “what is the value of the mentally accumulated evidence?”

span.label: frontal firing answers which choice the evidence so far favours, clustering into a positive and a negative group
span.quote: Despite the similarities between FOF and PPC based on trial-averaged responses ( Fig. 1c,d ), the tuning curve analysis revealed a very different encoding of the accumulator’s value a(t) in the FOF. Neurons in the FOF exhibited a more categorical mapping between firing rate and the sign of the accumulator value that tended to cluster into an a>0 and an a<0 group, while the mapping was again stable across time ( Fig. 3b ). The sign of a indicates the choice, so the FOF categorically encodes which of the two available choices is favored by the evidence accumulated so far. Thus, FOF responses can be approximately described as the categorical answer to the question “if the go signal came now, which choice should I make?”

span.label: the shorter click latency in frontal cortex suggests sensory information reaches it through circuits that bypass parietal cortex
span.quote: The longer mean latency of the click-triggered average in PPC (~200 ms) compared to FOF (~100 ms) suggests that sensory information in this task may reach the FOF through circuits that bypass the PPC.

span.label: the inactivation effect is modelled as converting a fraction of already-categorised contralateral choices into ipsilateral ones, which is a step after accumulation rather than during it
span.note: duplicate of: mechanisms[1]
span.quote: We defined “post-categorization bias” as a process that takes a fraction of the trials categorized as choices contralateral to the inactivated side of the brain, and converts them into ipsilateral choices.

span.label: There is no primate frontal eye field dataset against which the click-triggered-average result can be compared.
span.note: what this limits: the click-triggered-average result: NO EQUIVALENT EXPERIMENT FROM PRIMATE FEF EXISTS AS YET FOR COMPARISON
span.quote: No equivalent experiment from primate FEF exists as yet for comparison.

span.label: Data collection and analysis were not blinded to experimental group.
span.note: what this limits: every group comparison in the paper: INVESTIGATORS WERE NOT BLINDED TO EXPERIMENTAL GROUPS DURING DATA COLLECTION OR ANALYSIS
span.quote: Investigators were not blinded to experimental groups during data collection or analysis.

span.label: The 500 ms and 250 ms optogenetic groups were run sequentially, so group assignment was not randomised.
span.note: what this limits: the comparison between the two optogenetic durations: THE ASSIGNMENT OF GROUP WAS NOT RANDOMIZED - the groups were run sequentially
span.quote: Therefore, the assignment of group was not randomized.

span.label: Two rats were dropped from the fine-timing optogenetic analyses on the basis of their full-trial effects.
span.note: what this limits: the fine-timing optogenetic results: TWO RATS WERE NOT INCLUDED ... BECAUSE THEY DID NOT EXHIBIT SIGNIFICANT FULL-TRIAL EFFECTS - the exclusion criterion is the effect being measured
span.quote: However, two rats were not included in the higher temporal resolution optogenetic experiments because they did not exhibit significant full-trial effects.

span.label: investigators were not blinded to experimental groups during data collection or analysis
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - unblinded collection and analysis
span.quote: All statistical tests were made between groups with similar sample sizes. Investigators were not blinded to experimental groups during data collection or analysis.

span.label: two rats were dropped from the finer-timing experiments because they had not shown a significant full-trial effect, and the two timing groups were run sequentially so group assignment was not randomized
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 3 - selection on the outcome
span.quote: However, two rats were not included in the higher temporal resolution optogenetic experiments because they did not exhibit significant full-trial effects. The 500 ms and 250 ms experiments were performed sequentially in different groups of rats. Therefore, the assignment of group was not randomized.

span.label: the accumulator value used to build the tuning curves is estimated partly from the choice the animal went on to make
span.note: what this limits: every accumulator tuning curve: A BETTER ESTIMATE OF THE ACCUMULATED EVIDENCE CAN BE OBTAINED BY ALSO TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE CHOICE MADE AT THE END OF THE TRIAL - the regressor is informed by the outcome it is used to explain
span.quote: A better estimate of the accumulated evidence can be obtained by also taking into account the choice made at the end of the trial. This is calculated using the backward propagation of accumulator values that are consistent with that choice at the end of the stimulus presentation ( Extended Data Figure 2b ) 10 . We use this improved estimate that also takes into account subject

span.label: the encoding difference does not survive the end of the decision, since the parietal map becomes categorical during motor preparation
span.note: what this limits: the scope of the PPC/FOF encoding difference in time: THE DIFFERENCE IN ENCODING BETWEEN PPC AND FOF WAS NOT MAINTAINED AFTER THE END OF THE DECISION PROCESS
span.quote: The difference in encoding between PPC and FOF was not maintained after the end of the decision process. During the period of motor preparation, the FOF maintained a categorical encoding, while the graded encoding in the PPC converged to a categorical encoding

span.label: no comparable click-triggered measurement exists in the primate frontal eye fields for comparison
span.note: what this limits: the cross-species comparison: no comparable click-triggered measurement exists in the primate frontal eye fields, so the analogy is not tested against one
span.quote: We extracted the average influence of a single quantum of sensory evidence (a click) on the neural firing rates by computing the click-triggered average firing rate. Individual clicks have a measurable and sustained influence on PPC neural responses ( Fig. 1e ), consistent with the sustained effects of analogous manipulations in monkey PPC 16 . Individual clicks also produced a sustained influence on FOF neural responses, albeit with a magnitude that slowly but significantly decayed over several hundred milliseconds

span.label: preferred sides are mixed rather than uniformly contralateral, at about 59 percent in both areas
span.note: what this limits: any contralateral-preference claim: THE PREFERRED SIDE WAS CONTRALATERAL FOR 59.1% OF THE PPC NEURONS AND 59.4% OF THE FOF NEURONS - mixed selectivity, not a uniform map
span.quote: The preferred side was contralateral for 59.1% of the PPC neurons and 59.4% of the FOF neurons. We note that mixed selectivity like this in rat prefrontal cortex still yields ipsilateral biases after unilateral inactivation

span.label: a fitted trial-by-trial accumulator, used as the independent variable that neural responses are plotted against
span.quote: We used the behavioral model previously developed for this task 10 to obtain trial-by-trial, moment-by-moment estimates of the accumulating evidence, denoted by a(t) ( Extended Data Fig. 2 , Extended Data Table 1 ). Together with the simultaneously recorded firing rates r(t), this enabled the estimation of “tuning curves” that specify, for each point in time during the stimulus, how r depends on a

span.label: the click-triggered average, isolating one stimulus quantum's effect by subtracting the expected response for that Poisson rate
span.quote: Due to the Poisson nature of the stimulus, given an underlying click-generating Poisson rate, the presence of a click at one moment in time has no bearing on the probability of a click at other times. Therefore, if one aligns the residual response to a click, it describes the change in response associated with that click relative to the average expected response to clicks at other times. In this way, the residual response allowed us to isolate the effect of a single click apart from the confounding effect of the mean response across time for a given Poisson rate.

span.label: halorhodopsin silencing on a random quarter of trials, used to convert an encoding claim into a timing prediction
span.quote: Laser illumination occurred on a random 25% of trials. Behavioral bias was measured as the mean difference between the observed “go ipsi” rate for inactivation and control trials for each of 10 binned stimulus strengths. Thus, a positive value represents an increase in ipsilateral responses on laser illumination trials.

span.label: single-parameter variants of one behavioural model compared by bootstrapped likelihood ratio
span.quote: We performed statistical comparisons of the quality of the fits using a nonparametric resampling bootstrap procedure. We first generated 200 sets of trials with the same trial count as the original data by resampling the original data with replacement. We then fit each of these sets with the models described above and measured the difference in likelihood between post-categorization bias and the other alternatives for each resampled set of data. This provided a distribution of likelihood ratios from which we could estimate the statistical probability that post-categorization bias provides an improved fit compared to the other models.

span.label: MODEL-FREE analyses run alongside the model-based ones
span.note: eliminates: the accumulation model itself as the source of the conclusion - if only the fitted model showed gradual accumulation, the finding could be a property of the model rather than of the rats
span.quote: analyses were used to confirm that the rats were basing their decisions on evidence gradually accumulated throughout each stimulus period

span.label: THE STANDARD ANALYSIS SAYS THE TWO AREAS ARE THE SAME AND A DIFFERENT ANALYSIS ON THE SAME DATA SAYS THEY ARE NOT: trial-averaged ramping looks alike in both, and the tuning curve assay separates a graded code from a categorical one
span.quote: Classical analyses uncovered correlates of accumulating evidence, similar to previous observations in primates and also similar across the two regions. However, tuning curve assays revealed that while the PPC encodes a graded value of the accumulating evidence, the FOF has a more categorical encoding that indicates, throughout the trial, the decision provisionally favored by the evidence accumulated so far.

span.label: and the same firing rate is read as the answer to two different questions - what is the value of the accumulated evidence, against which choice should I make if the signal came now
span.quote: Despite the similarities between FOF and PPC based on trial-averaged responses ( Fig. 1c,d ), the tuning curve analysis revealed a very different encoding of the accumulator’s value a(t) in the FOF. Neurons in the FOF exhibited a more categorical mapping between firing rate and the sign of the accumulator value that tended to cluster into an a>0 and an a<0 group, while the mapping was again stable across time ( Fig. 3b ). The sign of a indicates the choice, so the FOF categorically encodes which of the two available choices is favored by the evidence accumulated so far. Thus, FOF responses can be approximately described as the categorical answer to the question “if the go signal came now, which choice should I make?”

span.label: THE RIVAL ACCOUNTS ARE SORTED BY WHEN THEY ACT: two of the four modelled biases must operate throughout accumulation and two only at its end, which is exactly what the timed silencing can separate
span.quote: We note that (3) and (4), unbalanced input gain and and unbalanced input noise, both imply mechanisms that act throughout the entirety of the accumulation process. In contrast, (1) and (2), the post-categorization bias and the accumulator shift, can be implemented via a mechanism that acts only at the end of the accumulation process.

span.label: so the model comparison and the causal experiment are testing the same distinction in two ways rather than checking each other
span.quote: Consistent with the idea that the FOF’s dominant role is to control the categorical choice, a model-based analysis indicated that a post-categorization bias explained these optogenetic inactivation data significantly better than alternative forms of bias that directly affected the accumulation process

span.label: THE STIMULUS IS DESIGNED SO THAT THE ANALYSIS IS VALID: because clicks come from a Poisson process, one click's timing says nothing about another's, which is what licenses the click-triggered average at all
span.quote: Due to the Poisson nature of the stimulus, given an underlying click-generating Poisson rate, the presence of a click at one moment in time has no bearing on the probability of a click at other times. Therefore, if one aligns the residual response to a click, it describes the change in response associated with that click relative to the average expected response to clicks at other times. In this way, the residual response allowed us to isolate the effect of a single click apart from the confounding effect of the mean response across time for a given Poisson rate.

span.label: THE LATENT VARIABLE IS INFERRED PARTLY FROM THE OUTCOME: the better estimate of accumulated evidence uses the choice the animal went on to make, and the frontal claim is about encoding that same choice
span.quote: A better estimate of the accumulated evidence can be obtained by also taking into account the choice made at the end of the trial. This is calculated using the backward propagation of accumulator values that are consistent with that choice at the end of the stimulus presentation ( Extended Data Figure 2b ) 10 . We use this improved estimate that also takes into account subject

span.label: ENCODING IS NOT NECESSITY: parietal cortex carries a veridical graded code for the accumulator, and the same laboratory reports that its activity is not needed for the behaviour
span.quote: PPC neurons veridically encode a graded value of the accumulated evidence, even though separate work from our laboratory suggests that PPC activity is not necessary for choice behavior in this task

span.label: the sample is declared unselected and then selected: every isolatable neuron was recorded regardless of response properties, and the analysis keeps the side-selective ones for a stated reason
span.quote: To examine whether signatures of evidence accumulation are present in the rodent brain, we recorded from 394 neurons in PPC of 4 rats and 397 neurons in FOF of 6 rats while they performed the Poisson Clicks task. These two areas that have been suggested as potential rat homologues of primate PPC and FEF 12 , 13 . We recorded all isolatable neurons encountered regardless of response properties.

span.label: and both disclosures are made - the recording area was assigned randomly, the timing groups were not
span.quote: However, two rats were not included in the higher temporal resolution optogenetic experiments because they did not exhibit significant full-trial effects. The 500 ms and 250 ms experiments were performed sequentially in different groups of rats. Therefore, the assignment of group was not randomized.

span.label: claim_type: mechanism
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: mechanism — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Contrary to current views 3 , 5 , 7 – 9 , this suggests that premotor activity in frontal cortex does not play a role in the accumulation process, but instead has a more categorical function, such as transforming accumulated evidence into a discrete choice.

span.label: method: tuning curves relating firing rate to a trial-by-trial estimate of the accumulator from a fitted behavioural model, compared between areas, and unilateral optogenetic silencing in four separate time windows
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: electrophysiology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.

Together with the simultaneously recorded firing rates r(t), this enabled the estimation of “tuning curves” that specify, for each point in time during the stimulus, how r depends on a

span.label: phenomenon: gradual accumulation of sensory evidence toward a binary choice, and its neural correlates in more than one cortical area
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: evidence accumulation in perceptual decision-making — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Side-selective neurons in both PPC and FOF exhibited average firing rates that were initially constant in time and then ramped upwards for stimuli in the preferred direction with a slope proportional to the stimulus strength. A similar but downwards ramping pattern was found for anti-preferred-direction stimuli ( Fig. 1c,d ; Extended Data Fig. 1d,e for single neuron examples). These response profiles are similar to those found in monkey LIP and FEF during visual motion discrimination tasks 3 – 5 , 11 , suggesting that rats and monkeys may use similar algorithms and related circuits to perform evidence accumulation.

span.label: contradicts → the prevailing view that prefrontal cortex is part of the neural circuit for evidence accumulation (refs 3, 5, 7, 8)
span.quote: These results suggest that accumulation occurs upstream to FOF and call into question the prevailing view that prefrontal cortex is part of the neural circuit for accumulation of evidence

span.label: builds-on → the previously developed "Poisson Clicks" accumulation task (ref. 10)
span.quote: We trained rats on a previously developed decision task in which subjects accumulate sensory evidence over many hundreds of milliseconds to inform a binary left-right choice (“Poisson Clicks” task, Fig. 1a , Extended Data Fig. 1a–c ) 10 .

span.label: replicates → previous findings of pre-movement side selectivity in rat PPC (refs 14, 15) and FOF (ref. 13)
span.quote: This pre-movement side selectivity is consistent with previous findings in both rat PPC 14 , 15 and FOF 13 .

span.label: contradicts → the prevailing view that prefrontal cortex is part of the circuit that accumulates evidence
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHEN IN THE TRIAL THE PERTURBATION MATTERS. 'Unilateral FOF perturbations AFFECT CHOICE BEHAVIOR ONLY AT THE END OF THE EVIDENCE ACCUMULATION PERIOD, when the provisional choice must be converted into a motor act.' The prevailing view is not denied a role for prefrontal cortex - it is denied the ACCUMULATION role, on the evidence of WHEN the effect appears. Q-444.
span.quote: Unilateral FOF perturbations affect choice behavior only at the end of the evidence accumulation period, when the provisional choice must be converted into a motor act. These results suggest that accumulation occurs upstream to FOF and call into question the prevailing view that prefrontal cortex is part of the neural circuit for accumulation of evidence

span.label: supports → primate work reporting ramping correlates of accumulation in parietal and frontal eye field neurons
span.quote: Side-selective neurons in both PPC and FOF exhibited average firing rates that were initially constant in time and then ramped upwards for stimuli in the preferred direction with a slope proportional to the stimulus strength. A similar but downwards ramping pattern was found for anti-preferred-direction stimuli ( Fig. 1c,d ; Extended Data Fig. 1d,e for single neuron examples). These response profiles are similar to those found in monkey LIP and FEF during visual motion discrimination tasks 3 – 5 , 11 , suggesting that rats and monkeys may use similar algorithms and related circuits to perform evidence accumulation.

span.label: extends → the graded parietal encoding seen in monkeys, which was measured in a task that did not require temporal accumulation
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER THE TASK REQUIRED TEMPORAL ACCUMULATION AT ALL. 'A SIMILAR ENCODING WAS OBSERVED IN MONKEY PPC, ALBEIT USING A TASK THAT DID NOT REQUIRE A TEMPORAL ACCUMULATION STRATEGY.' The earlier finding is granted in full and its task is named as lacking the thing this paper is about - so a `similar encoding` across species is a similarity of signal, not of computation, and only the task says which. Q-511.

A similar encoding was observed in monkey PPC, albeit using a task that did not require a temporal accumulation strategy 17 . Thus, during decision formation, firing rates in PPC change over time as the accumulated evidence changes, but at any timepoint the graded value of the accumulator is encoded, by a fixed map, into a graded firing rate. We computed the steepness of each neuron’s tuning curve, and while there was overlap between the PPC and the FOF populations, there was a significant shift towards greater steepness for the distribution of FOF neurons compared to PPC neurons

span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — 23 percent of parietal and 32 percent of frontal neurons qualify, kept because they are the ones most likely to matter for the decision
span.quote: Ninety-three neurons in PPC (23%) and 128 neurons in FOF (32%) exhibited firing rates during the pre-movement period (from stimulus onset to center port withdrawal) that were significantly different (p<0.05) for trials that subsequently ended with a right versus a left choice. This pre-movement side selectivity is consistent with previous findings in both rat PPC 14 , 15 and FOF 13 . We focus on these pre-movement side-selective neurons because they are most likely to play a role in decision formation.

span.quote: Side-selective neurons in both PPC and FOF exhibited average firing rates that were initially constant in time and then ramped upwards for stimuli in the preferred direction with a slope proportional to the stimulus strength. These response profiles are similar to those found in monkey LIP and FEF during visual motion discrimination tasks 3 – 5 , 11 , suggesting that rats and monkeys may use similar algorithms and related circuits to perform evidence accumulation.

span.quote: This analysis revealed that PPC encoded the accumulator’s evolving value a(t) using a graded map that is stable across time ( Fig. 3a ). A similar encoding was observed in monkey PPC, albeit using a task that did not require a temporal accumulation strategy 17 . Thus, during decision formation, firing rates in PPC change over time as the accumulated evidence changes, but at any timepoint the graded value of the accumulator is encoded, by a fixed map, into a graded firing rate. In this way, the firing rate provides the answer to the question “what is the value of the mentally accumulated evidence?”

Neurons in the FOF exhibited a more categorical mapping between firing rate and the sign of the accumulator value that tended to cluster into an a>0 and an a<0 group, while the mapping was again stable across time ( Fig. 3b ). The sign of a indicates the choice, so the FOF categorically encodes which of the two available choices is favored by the evidence accumulated so far. Thus, FOF responses can be approximately described as the categorical answer to the question “if the go signal came now, which choice should I make?”

In this way, the residual response allowed us to isolate the effect of a single click apart from the confounding effect of the mean response across time for a given Poisson rate.
